chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id al-Ahwazi, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Kharija, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has entrusted four thousand angels to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), dishevelled and covered in dust, who weep over him until the Day of Resurrection. So whoever visits him, cognizant of his right, they will escort him until they bring him to his place of safety. And if he falls ill, they will visit him morning and evening. And if he dies, they will attend his funeral and seek forgiveness for him until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.استغفروا: They seek forgiveness, indicating angelic intercession
key_terms.شعثا غبرا: Dishevelled and dusty, signifying perpetual mourning
key_terms.عارفا بحقه: Cognizant of his right, meaning recognizing Husayn's spiritual station
key_terms.مأمنه: His place of safety/shelter, referring to one's home or spiritual refuge
key_terms.وكل: Entrusted/appointed, indicating God's deliberate assignment of angels

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the angels at the grave of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes the angelic guardians assigned by God to the grave of Imam al-Husayn (AS) in Karbala. This hadith, narrated in a Muharram gathering in 368 AH, reflects the profound spiritual significance of the pilgrimage (ziyara) to Husayn's shrine, promising that those who visit with genuine recognition of his station will receive angelic protection throughout their lives and into death.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa from al-Husayn b. Sa`id al-Ahwazi from al Qasim b. Muhammad from Ishaq b. Ibrahim from Harun b. Kharija.  He said: I heard Abu `Abdillah say:

Allah has entrusted four thousand angels, dishevelled, covered in dust, to the grave of al-Husayn. They will weep over him till the Day of Resurrection. So, whoever visits him, cognizant of his right, they will escort him until they make him reach his shelter (home). And if he is sick, they will come to visit him, morning and evening. If he dies, they will attend his funeral and they will seek forgiveness for him until the Day of Resurrection.
